keywords_en: criminal; crime of accepting bribes; second instance; high people's court; Hainan Province; state organ; Criminal Law; Supplementary Provisions on Punishing the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery; whether it constitutes the crime of accepting bribes; evidentiary effect of handwritten confession; whether the defendant took advantage of his position to seek benefits; affirm the original judgment; internal employee shares; stock listing; bribery; securities
full_text_en:
Xin Yejiang — bribery

Defendant: Xin Yejiang, male, 63 years old, a native of Linli County, Hunan Province, former deputy director of the Standing Committee of the First People's Congress of Hainan Province. Pursuant to Article 30 of the Organic Law of the Local People's Congresses and Local People's Governments of the People's Republic of China, and following review and approval at the 26th session of the Standing Committee of the Hainan Provincial People's Congress on December 27, 1996, Xin Yejiang was arrested.

Defense Counsel: Zhao Jianping, Fan Lina, lawyers of Tianhai Law Firm.

The Haikou Municipal People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Haikou Intermediate People's Court, charging the defendant Xin Yejiang with bribery.

Allegations in the Indictment: The Haikou Municipal People's Procuratorate alleged: After accepting the payment for 50,000 internal employee shares of Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haiyao Company), the defendant Xin Yejiang took advantage of his position to seek benefits for the company. Xin Yejiang is charged with bribery, and it is requested that he be punished according to law.

Defendant's Defense: Xin Yejiang argued: My original confession that I accepted the payment for 50,000 internal employee shares of Haiyao Company was against my will; in fact, I paid the share subscription fee. I never said that I would help Haiyao Company's shares get listed, and when the Provincial Securities Commission met to recommend listed companies, I did not vote in favor of Haiyao Company. Signing the word "Agreed" on the submission documents was within the scope of my normal work. I did not seek benefits for Haiyao Company, and I do not constitute bribery.

Defense Counsel's Arguments: The defense counsel stated: The handwritten confession of Xin Yejiang was obtained illegally and cannot be used as evidence in this case; the testimony of witness Lin Danyang contains doubts as to the time and place of the share delivery and cannot be accepted; Xin Yejiang purchased shares rather than accepted bribes, and the indictment lacks sufficient evidence to charge Xin Yejiang with bribery; accordingly, a verdict of not guilty should be pronounced according to law.

Facts Found by the Haikou Intermediate People's Court: In May 1993, Haiyao Company entrusted Lin Danyang, manager of the business department of its subsidiary real estate development company, to establish connections for the listing of the company's shares. Lin Danyang then met Xin Yejiang, who was then deputy director of the Provincial Securities Commission, through a person surnamed Fu of Hainan Publishing House. Lin reported to Xin the situation of Haiyao Company's application for share listing and hoped that Xin Yejiang would provide support. Xin expressed that he could help. Subsequently, the leadership of Haiyao Company, based on Lin Danyang's request, decided to set aside 60,000 internal employee shares for relationship-building, but asked Lin to recover the share subscription payment as much as possible. Lin Danyang took his brother Lin Danqing's receipt for 10,000 yuan Haiyao Company share subscription, sold it on the black market for RMB 60,000, and paid this sum to Haiyao Company on July 21, 1993. He then collected the receipt for 60,000 yuan of internal employee shares, returned the 10,000 yuan share receipt to his brother, and delivered the other 50,000 yuan receipt for Haiyao Company internal employee shares registered in the name of Li Wucheng, along with Li Wucheng's ID card, to Xin Yejiang's home on the evening of late July 1993. Xin accepted it immediately without paying the subscription fee. Thereafter, on September 27, 1993, Xin Yejiang signed an opinion of "Agreed" on the Provincial Securities Commission's "Report on Agreeing to Submit the Application Materials of Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. to the State Securities Commission for Review." In April 1994, Xin Yejiang handed over the accepted share receipt to his second son, Xin Yilin, to handle the custody procedures. In June of the same year, after completing the custody procedures, Xin Yilin entrusted Xiao Qiang, an employee of Hainan Huihong Enterprise Co., Ltd., to sell the shares at Hainan Funan Securities Business Department (now restructured as the Securities Department of Hainan Development Bank). The proceeds totaled RMB 193,194.04, with 73 shares remaining in the account.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: Xin Yejiang's handwritten confession; testimony of witnesses Lin Danyang, Han Yudong, Hong Fuju, Chen Mingxing, Fu Cezhen, Lin Danqing, Yang Guizhuan, Huang Yifan, Xin Yilin, Wang Li, and Xiao Qiang; minutes of Haiyao Company's 12th regular meeting in 1993; share subscription application report; receipt for 50,000 internal employee shares registered in the name of Li Wucheng and a copy of the roster; custody receipt; shareholder fund and securities delivery lists from Funan National Investment Securities Department; and a copy of the "Report on Agreeing to Submit the Application Materials of Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. to the State Securities Commission for Review" issued by the Hainan Securities Commission. The facts are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient.

Opinion of the Haikou Intermediate People's Court: The handwritten confession voluntarily given by the defendant Xin Yejiang was obtained by the Supreme People's Procuratorate during its case investigation. After trial, the court confirmed that it was written by Xin Yejiang. The circumstances described in that confession are corroborated by the testimony of witness Lin Danyang and other evidence, and are sufficient to prove that Xin Yejiang accepted the receipt for 50,000 yuan in share subscription. As a state functionary, Xin Yejiang took advantage of his position as deputy director of the Hainan Provincial Securities Commission to accept the receipt for 50,000 yuan of Haiyao Company internal employee shares, which he later converted into cash proceeds of over RMB 190,000. His conduct violated Article 4, paragraph 1, and Article 5 of the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the Punishment of Embezzlement and Bribery Crimes, and constitutes the crime of bribery. He should be punished in accordance with Article 2, paragraph 1, item (1) of those Supplementary Provisions, which prescribes a statutory sentence of "fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." Article 12 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which came into effect on October 1, 1997, provides: "If an act committed before the entry into force of this Law was deemed a crime under the law then in force, and if prosecution is not barred under Section 8 of Chapter IV of the General Provisions of this Law, criminal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the law then in force; however, if this Law does not deem the act a crime or imposes a lighter penalty, this Law shall apply." Xin Yejiang's conduct violates Article 385, paragraph 1, and Article 386 of the Criminal Law regarding the crime of bribery, and should be punished under Article 383, paragraph (2), which provides: "If the amount of personal embezzlement is not less than RMB 50,000 but less than RMB 100,000, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years, and may also be sentenced to confiscation of property." In comparison, the penalty under the Criminal Law is lighter, and the Criminal Law should be applied to Xin Yejiang. Pursuant to Article 64 of the Criminal Law, Xin Yejiang's illegal gains shall be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury. The arguments of Xin Yejiang and his defense counsel that he purchased shares, that the handwritten confession was illegally obtained, and that the confession was made against his will are inconsistent with the facts and cannot be sustained. After accepting the receipt for 50,000 yuan in shares, Xin Yejiang signed an opinion of "Agreed" on the Provincial Securities Commission's "Report on Agreeing to Submit the Application Materials of Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. to the State Securities Commission for Review." This is confirmed by a copy of that report and Xin Yejiang's confession at trial. His defense that "he did not use his official position to seek benefits for Haiyao Company" is also inconsistent with the facts and will not be accepted. Accordingly, on May 26, 1998, the Haikou Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant Xin Yejiang is convicted of bribery and sentenced to five years' imprisonment.

2. The illegal gains from Xin Yejiang's bribery, totaling RMB 193,192.04, and 73 shares of Haiyao Company stock, shall be recovered and turned over to the State Treasury.

After the judgment of first instance was pronounced, the defendant Xin Yejiang refused to accept it and appealed to the Hainan High People's Court on the same grounds.

Facts Found by the Hainan High People's Court: The facts found at first instance that Lin Danyang gave the receipt for 50,000 yuan in shares to the appellant Xin Yejiang, and that Xin did not pay for it, are confirmed by the testimony of witness Lin Danyang and the handwritten confession voluntarily written by Xin Yejiang when he confessed; the testimony and the confession correspond. The fact that Haiyao Company decided to set aside internal employee shares to establish connections for its stock listing is confirmed by the minutes of Haiyao Company's 12th regular meeting on May 22, 1993, and the testimony of Lin Danyang, Haiyao Company's Chairman and General Manager Han Yudong, Vice-Chairman Hong Fuju, and Deputy General Manager Chen Mingxing. The fact that Lin Danyang paid RMB 60,000 to the company and collected the receipt for 60,000 yuan in shares is confirmed by Lin Danyang's application report, the document processing card signed by Haiyao Company's leadership, the 60,000 yuan receipt, the receipt for 50,000 internal employee shares registered in Li Wucheng's name, a copy of the roster, and the testimony of witnesses Lin Danyang, Yang Guizhuan of Haiyao Company's Finance Department, and Huang Yifan of the Archives Office. The fact that Xin Yejiang handed over the accepted share receipt to Xin Yilin for custody, and that Xin Yilin entrusted Xiao Qiang to sell the shares, yielding proceeds of over RMB 190,000, is confirmed by the custody receipt, the shareholder fund and securities delivery lists from Funan National Investment Securities Department, the testimony of witnesses Xin Yilin, Wang Li, and Xiao Qiang, and Xin Yejiang's confession. The fact that Xin Yejiang used his official position to seek benefits for Haiyao Company is confirmed by copies of two documents: the Hainan Securities Commission's "Approval on Transforming Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. from a Targeted Offering Company into a Public Company and Issuing Shares to the Public," on which Xin Yejiang signed the opinion "Propose approval, please submit to Governor Wang for verification and issuance"; and the "Report on Agreeing to Submit the Application Materials of Hainan Haiyao Industrial Co., Ltd. to the State Securities Commission for Review."

Opinion of the Hainan High People's Court: The facts of bribery by the appellant Xin Yejiang found by the lower court are clear, and the evidence is reliable and sufficient. As a state functionary, Xin Yejiang took advantage of his official position to accept a receipt for RMB 50,000 in Haiyao Company internal employee shares, entrusted others to cash them out, and obtained proceeds of over RMB 190,000. His conduct constitutes the crime of bribery. The lower court correctly determined the conviction, properly applied the law, imposed an appropriate sentence, and followed lawful trial procedures. The appellant Xin Yejiang's grounds for appeal cannot be sustained. Accordingly, on June 16, 1998, the Hainan High People's Court, pursuant to Article 189, item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled as follows: Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.
